haiku-low.q1: Held for 10 minutes. If not claimed in time, the Inventory sweeper marks it EXPIRED and returns the stock to sale.
haiku-low.q2: Before the charge. If one line is short, Inventory writes nothing, Order sets FAILED_SHORT_STOCK, short items are shown, nothing is charged, cart unchanged.
haiku-low.q3: The order id is the idempotency key. Payment's unique payment row per order id and the provider's Idempotency-Key return the same payment, not a second charge.
haiku-low.q4: Order is set to CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK. Payment refunds the full amount, the customer gets a cancellation and refund email, and the order stays cancelled.
haiku-low.q5: On OrderConfirmed, Cart removes only the ordered lines still unchanged. On failed checkout (short stock or decline), the cart is unchanged.
haiku-low.q6: The Order service drives the flow. Its orders table, including order_status_history, records how far each checkout has got.
haiku-low.q7: The provider sends a webhook to Payment, which checks the signature and writes an outbox event. The relay publishes it to the broker for Order. A watchdog polls after 35 minutes without a webhook.
haiku-low.q8: Payment records each event id in webhook_events with a unique constraint. Repeats are acknowledged and change nothing, and racing copies are resolved by that constraint.
haiku-low.q9: Order sets FAILED_PAYMENT and makes one release call to Inventory, triggered by the PaymentDeclined outbox event. If no answer, it is not retried; the sweeper frees the hold within 10 minutes.
haiku-low.q10: Order asks Inventory to claim. If the hold lapsed, Inventory tries once to re-reserve and claim the same lines. If the lines are still free, fulfil; otherwise refund.
haiku-low.q11: Payment retries with backoff using the same key. After the last attempt the row becomes REFUND_FAILED and an ops alert is raised. Pending refunds are tracked in the refunds table.
haiku-low.q12: The OrderConfirmed event from Order causes the Cart service to remove the ordered lines still unchanged, idempotent on order id.

sonnet.q1: Held for 10 minutes. If not claimed, the sweeper (every minute) marks the HELD reservation EXPIRED and the stock goes back on sale. A later claim can still try to re-reserve the same lines once.
sonnet.q2: Reserved before the charge. If any line is short, nothing is written, no hold or charge is made, Inventory returns the short items (409), Order sets FAILED_SHORT_STOCK, the customer sees the short items and the cart is unchanged.
sonnet.q3: Every call uses the order id as idempotency key. Payment's payment row is unique on order id, so a lost reply returns the same payment, and the provider is charged with Idempotency-Key = order id, so the charge is done once.
sonnet.q4: Order sets CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK and writes an OrderCancelledOutOfStock event and cancellation email. Payment then refunds the full amount (refund row REFUND_PENDING, then SUCCEEDED). The order stays cancelled; the customer gets a cancellation and refund email.
sonnet.q5: The cart is emptied only on success, after OrderConfirmed: Cart removes ordered lines still matching the snapshot (later edits stay). On any failure (short stock, declined payment) the cart is unchanged and the customer can retry.
sonnet.q6: Order drives the flow. The record of progress is the order's status (PENDING_STOCK, AWAITING_PAYMENT, etc.) in Order's database, with order_status_history.
sonnet.q7: The provider sends a webhook to Payment (or the watchdog polls the provider after 35 minutes with no webhook). Payment updates the payment row and writes an outbox row in the same transaction; the relay publishes PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined to the broker, which Order consumes.
sonnet.q8: Payment checks the signature, then looks up the event id in webhook_events; if present, it acknowledges and changes nothing. New event ids are recorded under a unique constraint so racing copies process only once. Changes are also applied only if the payment is in the expected state (guarded update). Order acts only while AWAITING_PAYMENT.
sonnet.q9: The PaymentDeclined event from Payment's outbox triggers Order, if AWAITING_PAYMENT, to set FAILED_PAYMENT and make one non-retried call to Inventory to release the hold (HELD becomes RELEASED, stock back on sale). If no answer, the sweeper frees it within 10 minutes.
sonnet.q10: On PaymentSucceeded, Order asks Inventory to claim. If the hold expired or was swept, Inventory tries once to re-reserve and claim the same lines in one transaction. If the lines are still free, the claim succeeds and the order is confirmed; otherwise the claim is refused, the order is cancelled and fully refunded.
sonnet.q11: It is retried with backoff using the same key. After the last attempt the refund becomes REFUND_FAILED and an ops alert is raised; the row stays open until someone resolves it. The pending refund is tracked in Payment's refunds table (REFUND_PENDING row saved before calling the provider).
sonnet.q12: The OrderConfirmed event (written to Order's outbox when status becomes CONFIRMED) is consumed by the Cart service, which removes the ordered lines still unchanged from the snapshot. Cart does it, idempotent on order id.
